questions.explanation: The note defines a computer as an electronic device capable of input, processing, output, and storage.

questions.stem: Which of the following operations would NOT typically be handled directly by the ALU?
questions.explanation: The ALU handles arithmetic and logical operations, not storage tasks.

questions.stem: In the computer data flow process, what is the result of processing called?
questions.explanation: The processed result is conventionally referred to as output or information.

questions.stem: Which storage device would retain data even after the system is powered off?
questions.explanation: SSD is non-volatile storage, unlike RAM, cache, and registers.

questions.stem: Which two major parts is a computer basically divided into?
questions.explanation: The note explicitly states that a computer is divided into hardware and software.

questions.stem: Which scenario BEST demonstrates the concept of versatility in computers?

options.A: A computer performing calculations very fast
options.B: A computer running multiple different types of applications
options.C: A computer storing large amounts of data
options.D: A computer operating continuously without rest

questions.explanation: Versatility refers to the ability to perform different kinds of tasks.

questions.stem: The relationship between hardware and software is compared to which human attributes?
questions.explanation: Hardware is likened to the body, while software is compared to the spirit or soul.

questions.stem: Which component would MOST directly affect how many bits a CPU can process at once?
questions.explanation: Word size determines how many bits a CPU can process in a single operation.

questions.stem: Why is software described as intangible?

options.B: Because it exists independently of hardware
options.C: Because it cannot be physically touched

questions.explanation: Software is intangible as it consists of programs and instructions, not physical components.

questions.stem: A system is designed to respond instantly to sensor input within strict time limits. What type of computing is this?
questions.explanation: Real-time computing operates within strict timing constraints.

questions.stem: In what form do computers fundamentally process data?
questions.explanation: The note states that computers process data in binary digital format.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why transistors replaced vacuum tubes?

options.A: They were larger and easier to repair
options.C: They were smaller, faster, and more efficient

questions.explanation: Transistors improved size, efficiency, and reliability compared to vacuum tubes.

questions.stem: Machine language differs from human-readable languages primarily because it is based on:
questions.explanation: Machine language is based on binary (0s and 1s), unlike human-readable languages.

questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST likely require a workstation instead of a standard PC?
questions.explanation: Workstations are designed for high-performance tasks like simulations and engineering work.

questions.stem: Which capability allows computers to solve repetitive computational jobs efficiently?

options.B: Software capability with high accuracy and timeliness

questions.explanation: The note attributes repetitive job efficiency to software capability, accuracy, and timeliness.

questions.stem: Which component acts as a temporary high-speed buffer between the CPU and main memory?
questions.explanation: Cache memory stores frequently used data for faster access by the CPU.

questions.stem: A computer system is best described as:

options.A: Only the hardware components of a computer
options.C: A combination of hardware, software, and users

questions.explanation: The note defines a computer system as involving hardware, software, and users.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the role of an operating system?

options.B: It acts as an interface between hardware, software, and users

questions.explanation: The OS manages communication between hardware, software, and users.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as part of a full-fledged computer system?
questions.explanation: The ideal computer system includes users, application software, system software, OS, and hardware.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an embedded system?
questions.explanation: Embedded systems perform dedicated functions within larger systems.

questions.stem: Why is the hardware subsystem considered the bedrock of other subsystems?

options.C: Because other subsystems depend on it to function

questions.explanation: The note emphasizes hardware as the foundational layer supporting other subsystems.

questions.stem: If a computer can handle multiple tasks simultaneously by splitting them across cores, what is this process called?
questions.explanation: Multithreading splits tasks into smaller parts to run concurrently on multiple cores.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a computer?
questions.explanation: Consistency is explicitly listed as a characteristic of computers.

questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST improve system performance when running many applications at once?
questions.explanation: More RAM allows more applications to run simultaneously without slowing down.

questions.stem: Which characteristic refers to a computer’s ability to perform tasks accurately without fatigue?
questions.explanation: Diligence means the computer can work continuously without loss of performance.

questions.stem: Which network component is responsible for directing data packets between different networks?
questions.explanation: Routers forward data packets between different networks.

questions.stem: Computer hardware is best defined as:

options.B: Any physical component contributing to a computer system

questions.explanation: The lecture defines hardware as the physical parts of a computer system.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly differentiates hardware from software?

options.A: Hardware is intangible while software is tangible
options.B: Hardware provides instructions while software executes them
options.C: Hardware can be touched while software cannot
options.D: Hardware depends on software to exist physically

questions.explanation: The distinction is based on tangibility as described in the note.

questions.stem: Which classification groups computers based on processing power and physical size?
questions.explanation: The note categorizes computers by size, purpose, and type, including power and size.

questions.stem: Which feature best describes personal computers (PCs)?
questions.explanation: The note highlights PCs as common, cheaper, single-user, and versatile.

questions.stem: Why do laptops generally consume less power than desktop PCs?
questions.explanation: The reduced power consumption is due to miniaturized internal components.

questions.stem: Which type of computer is more powerful than a PC but still single-user?
questions.explanation: Workstations are single-user computers with higher specifications than PCs.

questions.stem: Minicomputers are best characterized as:
questions.explanation: The note states that minicomputers support multiple users simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes mainframe computers from minicomputers?

options.B: Support for thousands of users simultaneously

questions.explanation: Mainframes support far more users concurrently than minicomputers.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes supercomputers?

options.A: They are smaller versions of mainframes
options.B: They are designed for routine office tasks
options.C: They perform extremely high-speed, data-intensive computations
options.D: They are mainly used for word processing

questions.explanation: Supercomputers are built to solve grand challenge, computation-intensive problems.

questions.stem: Which technological advancement enabled modern supercomputers to exist?
questions.explanation: The note links supercomputer capabilities to improvements in chip technology.

questions.stem: A microchip is best described as:

options.B: A set of electronic circuits etched on silicon
options.C: A storage medium made from plastic

questions.explanation: The lecture defines microchips as electronic circuits mounted on silicon slabs.

questions.stem: Why is silicon preferred over metals in chip manufacturing?

options.D: Silicon conducts electricity better than copper

questions.explanation: As a semiconductor, silicon’s conductivity can be modified, unlike metals.

questions.stem: What does Moore’s Law primarily predict?

options.B: The cost of computers halves every year
options.C: The number of transistors on a chip doubles about every two years
options.D: Memory capacity remains constant over time

questions.explanation: Moore’s Law forecasts the doubling of transistor density approximately every two years.

questions.stem: Which outcome is a direct implication of Moore’s Law?
questions.explanation: The law implies smaller transistors and more powerful, compact chips.

questions.stem: Which future chip technology is expected to succeed transistor miniaturization?
questions.explanation: The note states future designs will rely on parallelism, 3D, and multi-core technologies.

questions.stem: Why is regular computer maintenance important?

options.C: To extend device lifespan and ensure optimal performance

questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes maintenance for efficiency, longevity, and reliability.

questions.stem: Which description best defines a computer network?

options.A: A single computer connected to peripheral devices
options.B: A system of interconnected computers and hardware for sharing data and resources
options.C: A collection of software programs running on one machine
options.D: A wireless communication system used only for Internet access

questions.explanation: A computer network is defined as multiple computers and computing hardware interconnected to share data, information, and resources.

questions.stem: In a computer network, what role does a server primarily play?

options.A: It converts analog signals to digital signals
options.B: It stores files and resources that can be accessed by other computers
options.D: It acts as a gateway between wireless networks

questions.explanation: The note explains that files and documents can be created, saved, and stored on a server and accessed by other computers on the network.

questions.stem: What term is used to describe computers connected on a network?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that computers on a network are called nodes or hosts.

questions.stem: Why must multiple wired or wireless paths in a network be carefully designed?

options.A: To reduce the cost of network devices
options.B: To enable reliable sending and receiving of data
options.C: To eliminate the need for network protocols
options.D: To increase the physical size of the network

questions.explanation: The note emphasizes that paths must be carefully designed to enable sending and receiving data as required.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is primarily responsible for directing data between networks?
questions.explanation: Routers are listed as network-enabled equipment that support communication over long ranges by directing data between networks.

questions.stem: Which key difference distinguishes a modem from a network card?

options.A: A modem sends data over a network cable, while a network card uses phone lines
options.B: A modem sends information over a communication line, while a network card sends over a network cable
options.C: A modem is used only in LANs, while a network card is used only in WANs
options.D: A modem is faster and more reliable than a network card

questions.explanation: The lecture directly compares their roles, highlighting the transmission medium used by each.

questions.stem: Which limitation of modems is identified in the lecture note?

options.B: Susceptibility to phone line static and slower speed

questions.explanation: The note states that modems are usually slow and susceptible to problems such as phone line static.

questions.stem: Which component allows a computer to connect to a LAN or ISP through a cable modem or DSL?
questions.explanation: The lecture explains that network cards connect computers to LANs or ISPs via cable modem or DSL.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a basic requirement of a computer network?
questions.explanation: The note lists network software, protocols, transmission media, devices, and multiple computers, not application software alone.

questions.stem: Which cable type is identified as the most commonly used network communication medium?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that ethernet cables are the most commonly used network cables.

questions.stem: Which connector is commonly associated with Category 5 and Category 6 Ethernet cables?
questions.explanation: The note specifies that CAT 5 and CAT 6 Ethernet cables use RJ-45 connectors.

questions.stem: Which type of network is designed for data transmission among personal devices using Bluetooth or Wi-Fi?
questions.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) is defined as connecting personal devices using Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or TCP/IP.

questions.stem: Which network type interconnects computers within a limited geographical area such as a school or office?
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) connects computers within a local place or area.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) from a traditional LAN?

options.B: It integrates two or more LANs into a shared segment

questions.explanation: A VLAN involves two or more LANs configured and integrated to share resources.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly characterizes a Wide Area Network (WAN)?

options.A: It connects devices within a single room
options.B: It extends over a large geographical region using leased circuits
options.C: It is limited to personal devices

questions.explanation: WANs extend over large geographical regions and are often established with leased telecommunication circuits.

questions.stem: Why is the Internet considered a WAN?

options.A: Because it connects only private networks
options.B: Because it is restricted to academic institutions
options.C: Because it spans large geographical areas and connects many networks
options.D: Because it uses only wireless technology

questions.explanation: The Internet is described as a worldwide interconnection of many network types, fitting the definition of a WAN.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a Storage Area Network (SAN)?
questions.explanation: SANs provide access to large integrated arrays or block-level data storage.

questions.stem: What feature allows users of a WLAN to remain connected while moving within a coverage area?
questions.explanation: WLANs use high-frequency radio waves, enabling mobility within the coverage area.

questions.stem: Which characteristic best defines an intranet?
questions.explanation: An intranet is a dedicated and classified network strictly within an organization.

questions.stem: How does an extranet differ from an intranet?

options.B: It allows controlled access to authorized external parties

questions.explanation: An extranet permits access to specific authorized external bodies without exposing the entire network.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?

options.B: To extend a private network over a public network securely

questions.explanation: A VPN enables users to send and receive data over public networks as if directly connected to a private network.

questions.stem: What defines a peer-to-peer (P2P) network?
questions.explanation: In P2P networks, peers are equally privileged and share workloads.

questions.stem: Which type of maintenance is performed to prevent hardware failures before they occur?
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is done proactively to avoid hardware failures.

questions.stem: Corrective maintenance is primarily performed when:
questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance addresses hardware faults after they occur.

questions.stem: Predictive maintenance aims to:

options.B: Predict potential hardware failures before they happen

questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance uses monitoring to anticipate failures.

questions.stem: Which tools are commonly used for computer hardware maintenance?

options.A: Anti-static wrist strap, screwdrivers, compressed air

questions.explanation: These are standard tools for safely maintaining and cleaning computer hardware.

questions.stem: Why is it important to use an anti-static wrist strap when handling computer components?

options.B: To prevent electrostatic discharge that can damage components

questions.explanation: Static electricity can destroy sensitive hardware parts, and wrist straps prevent this.

questions.stem: Which environmental factor is critical to maintaining computer hardware?
questions.explanation: High temperature or humidity can damage hardware; proper environmental control is essential.

questions.stem: What is a common sign that a hardware component might be failing?

options.B: Unexpected shutdowns, strange noises, or performance slowdown

questions.explanation: These symptoms often indicate hardware issues.

questions.stem: Which practice ensures the safe backup and storage of computer data?

options.B: Using cloud storage and external drives regularly

questions.explanation: Regular backups on reliable media prevent data loss during hardware failures.

questions.stem: Why is regular cleaning of dust from computer hardware important?

options.B: Prevents overheating and prolongs component life

questions.explanation: Dust can block airflow and cause overheating, leading to hardware damage.
